failure_summary.description: Search or filter results were not consistently bound and saved to cache.
Calls used an unsupported amenity name or omitted/malformed an explicitly requested hotel constraint.
A round trip was represented as one outbound search with an arrival date instead of separate reversed legs.
The plan invented hotel dates and skipped a restaurant search whose required city was available.
The plan treated cached results for an earlier cuisine preference as satisfying a corrected request.

patch.reasoning: Most failures already contradict explicit skill rules on persistence, schemas, round trips, and missing inputs, so repeating those rules would not patch a content gap. Clarify how explicit corrections affect cache compatibility to prevent stale refinements from suppressing a newly requested action.

edits.target: - A cached base result does not satisfy a newly requested constraint, and a result for one domain does not satisfy a request for another. Use `print("No planning needed")` only when relevant, valid cached results already satisfy every requested action and constraint.
edits.content: - Treat explicit correction or replacement language (for example, “actually,” “instead,” or “only”) as superseding the conflicting earlier criterion while retaining nonconflicting context. Recheck cache coverage against the revised criterion: a refinement based on the superseded value is incompatible and cannot justify “No planning needed.” Use a compatible earlier base result for refinement only when it covers the remaining criteria; otherwise search with the revised criteria.
